name: DANA INCORPORATED INC

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That refusing is lazy, because unlike an all-cash deal this one leaves Dana holders owning equity in a going concern whose pro forma economics the companies have published. Eaton Mobility at $5.1 billion on about $1.7 billion of combined fully synergised adjusted EBITDA, with Dana holders at 49.9%, is arithmetic a careful analyst could do - and the multiples table on the brief blends to $28.95 against a $28.23 price, a +2.6% gap, which at least says the name is not mispriced.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Whether the multiples table is usable, since it is the only numeric comparator the brief offers.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and it fails the standing refusal test on three counts at once. The ev_gross_profit row returns NEGATIVE values at every percentile (-$7.56, -$5.21, -$1.06) because at cohort gross-profit multiples of 1.2x to 4.6x the implied enterprise value is below Dana's roughly $1.0 billion of net debt - and a negative row disqualifies the blend under the RIOT and EPRT rule. The cohort is explicitly 'not ranked - too few comparable Consumer Discretionary names'. And the trailing denominators describe a company that no longer exists: revenue stepped from $10.28 billion to $7.50 billion on the Off-Highway divestiture, so every trailing multiple is measured on a business 27% larger than today's, which is the MXL objection. The +2.6% blend is three disqualifications averaged into a decimal point. As for the pro forma arithmetic, the counter is right that it is doable and wrong that this engine should publish it: a fair value for Dana today requires a view on deal completion, on where Eaton Mobility's standalone EBITDA actually sits, and on the final share count - none of which is a reverse DCF, and all of which the schema has no field for.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Deal completion risk and the final capital structure. I did not read the Form S-4 or the Form 425 series beyond the announcement exhibits, so I have not verified the outside date, the condition set, the break fees or the regulatory posture; and the $1.1 billion cash distribution is 'subject to adjustments for cash and indebtedness', so the closing leverage is not yet fixed. I also could not establish why recorded EBIT is -$32 million.

what_changed: Two structural transactions inside twelve months, neither of which the engine knows about. First, Dana divested its Off-Highway business: revenue_series steps from $10,284 million to $7,500 million between the two newest years, equity_now is $1,920 million against an equity_series[0] of $840 million (2.29x), and total debt is down to $1,357 million - the gain and the deleveraging land in the first half of 2026, after the fiscal year the cash-flow history describes. Second, the pending Eaton Mobility combination announced 2026-06-11, closing expected in the first quarter of 2027 and reported on track as of September 2026, under which Eaton receives a cash distribution of about $1.1 billion funded through NEW DEBT raised prior to closing. Byron Foster became CEO on 2026-07-01. Operationally, Q2 2026 sales were $2,010 million against $1,935 million with a net LOSS of $5 million, full-year sales guidance was raised to $7.65-7.85 billion while adjusted EPS guidance was lowered, and $250 million of Eaton synergies are targeted within 24 months of closing.
consensus_case: At $28.23 Dana is not a standalone company being valued, it is half of a pending combination. On 2026-06-11 Dana agreed to combine with Eaton's Mobility Group in a Reverse Morris Trust: Eaton first separates Mobility to its own shareholders by split-off or spin-off, then Dana merges with a Mobility subsidiary and SURVIVES AS A WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY of the Mobility Group, with EATON shareholders owning at least 50.1% and Dana shareholders about 49.9% of the combined company. The price is therefore an opinion about a $5.1 billion transaction - roughly 8.3x estimated 2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA before synergies, 5.9x including $250 million of run-rate synergies - producing a company with about $11 billion of sales and $1.7 billion of adjusted EBITDA on a fully synergised pro forma basis, targeting $14-15 billion of sales and 18% margins by 2030. The stock is up 44.5% over twelve months on that, plus a 2026 sales guidance raise to $7.65-7.85 billion and resumed buybacks.
base_case_rationale: No growth rate and no fair value are supplied, and the refusal has nothing to do with the reason the engine failed. The engine returned status model_failed on `speculative_cost_of_debt_at_31%_debt_weight_wacc_unreliable`, which is triggered by a recorded EBIT of -$32 million - itself almost certainly a missing or charge-laden concept, since -0.4% of $7.5 billion of revenue fails the HP test for a company reporting a 10.3% segment margin in the quarter. Had that gate not fired, the model would have run a standalone discounted cash flow on a company that has contracted to become a 49.9% minority of something else. Every input would have been wrong: the three-year cash-flow history (cfo-less-capex of $298 million, $70 million and -$25 million) describes a company that still owned Off-Highway; the 107,576,679 share count will roughly double at closing when Eaton holders receive at least 50.1%; and enterprise value omits the roughly $1.1 billion of new debt to be raised before close. A valuation of Dana today is a merger-arbitrage and pro-forma-accretion exercise, not a cash-flow exercise, and the engine computes neither.
key_risks: Pending Reverse Morris Trust: Eaton shareholders take at least 50.1% and Dana shareholders about 49.9%, so the share count roughly doubles and Dana survives as a subsidiary of the Mobility Group
Eaton receives about $1.1bn of cash funded through NEW debt raised before closing - absent from the current enterprise value
The three-year cash-flow history describes a company that still owned the divested Off-Highway business (revenue $10.28bn to $7.50bn)
Recorded EBIT of -$32M on $7.5bn of revenue is -0.4% and fails the HP missing-concept test; it is what triggered the engine's refusal, for the wrong reason
The multiples blend of +2.6% is void: a negative ev_gross_profit row, an unranked cohort, and trailing denominators 27% too large
Q2 2026 was a net loss of $5M, and adjusted EPS guidance was lowered even as sales guidance was raised
watch_for: Closing of the Eaton Mobility combination, expected Q1 2027, and the final share count and net debt at close
S-4 effectiveness and the shareholder votes
Whether the $250M of run-rate synergies is reaffirmed at each quarter
Commercial-vehicle demand, which drove the Q2 margin improvement
Whether selection gates on form 425 - Dana has filed several, so the REFI form-type test would catch this name before it spends another slot
